goals.text: A written, evidence-backed review (REV artifact in .project/) of Slice 1 against PLAN-0001 §9 / PLAN-0002 and SPEC-0001..0014
Findings ranked by impact for: spec adherence, soundness/wiring/bugs, docs currency, duplication, unified TUI appearance, extending-pig UI/UX standards
Gates (check/race) observed and reported; no code changes unless the user asks

report.outcome: Orientation done; review tree with 6 areas / 28 leaf tasks created.

subtasks.title: Read inventory, probes, handoffs, skills (extending-pig, dot-project) and map code layout

report.outcome: Read PLAN-0001 (scope, §6 ambient contract, §9 ownership), PLAN-0002 (phases, exit, mode matrix), the Slice 1 inventory (self-attested 24/24 rows, 4 non-passing sub-anchors, named host limits) and extending-pig SKILL + ui-ux.md + dashboard-standard.md. Repo: ~86k Go lines, internal/host is 17.5k non-test lines in ~159 files; no BACKLOG.md and no .project/backlog/ exist although AGENTS.md references them; .project has no reviews/ dir yet. Task tree populated.
decisions: Review only, no code changes — user asked for comparison/review/gap analysis

Standards to check UI against: ui-ux.md header grammar (glyph, target, metrics joined by ' · '), three densities, nine-line dashboard frame, fixed height, no single-key actions, KeyHint labels, theme tokens only, config rule 7

acceptanceCriteria.text: Seam contract findings vs SPEC-0001 recorded

report.outcome: All 14 specs compared; findings in ~/.cache/pig-workbench-test-tmp/findings.md. Top: bash refuses any command containing a registered scheme prefix incl. http/https (critical); frame ledger lifetime 2 MiB wall; paths[] reads skip instruction discovery; session root listing fails beyond 16 entries; system-prompt resource stub; host skills absent from skill tree; 65/100 settings inert; several spec routes/resources missing.

SPEC-0001: diagnostics resources (cfg://workbench/integrations, docs://workbench/schemes) exist; method/event drifts recorded in 3.3. Side discovery: 65/100 catalog settings are inert ('unavailable'), incl. Slice-1-scope keys such as prompt.template; and a live false positive of the bash scheme-command detector hit this very session (to reproduce in 4.8).

SPEC-0002: admission, dedup, coalescing, expiry, limits, envelope and wake rules are implemented as specified. HIGH defect proven by a throwaway test: the 2 MiB body budget counts every frame ever admitted in the session lineage (terminal records never release), so a long session eventually fails every context-frame admission and third-party publish. Details in findings file.
open: Verify in 4.7 whether Read with paths[] registers instruction touches (live observation suggests not)

report.outcome: SPEC-0003 data contract (strict decoder, bounds, lifecycle, ownership check, settings) is implemented and well tested; no new drift found in §2-§6. While working, discovered and live-reproduced a CRITICAL bash defect: any command text containing a registered non-locatable scheme prefix incl. http/https is refused (curl URL, grep for scheme strings, echo, heredocs). Recorded with file:line in findings.
open: 5.1 must compare host/own_tools_render.go (own ten tools) with host/presentation_render.go (contributed tools): two render paths
Findings-file appends must not contain scheme+colon-slash-slash text (bash refuses the command)

report.outcome: SPEC-0004 live spot checks through the real tools: retired scheme answers with replacement (ok), cfg and job trees list, https read works with a path. Gaps: session self/frames and self/instructions/ are not readable, bare-origin https URL is refused, docs workbench/schemes/ empty listing prints nothing. Recorded in findings.

SPEC-0005 verified live through the real edit tool on scratch files (~/.cache/pig-workbench-test-tmp/edit): block replace, cross-file CUT/paste, CRLF, unseen-line guard and stale-tag relocation work. Only low findings (error wording, silent recovery, paste form undocumented in the tool description, known G5.2 deviation not written back to the spec).

SPEC-0006 verified live: selectors, literal punctuation filenames, multi-read with per-target errors, summaries, grep/find/ls bounded output all correct. One low wording finding. Observed: a single-path Read and a Grep under internal/host delivered internal/AGENTS.md and host/AGENTS.md frames; the earlier paths[] read of .project/plans did not deliver nested AGENTS.md (to test in 4.7).

SPEC-0007: ancestors placement, host files and single-path touches work live. HIGH: read with paths[] never triggers instruction discovery (instruction_context.go:136 reads only input["path"]), live-confirmed twice. Not re-verified here: pins, caps, diff updates (covered by the project's own live tests).
open: Integration job finished: FAIL, one test (TestLiveTrustPanelAddsAndRemovesARulePersistently); task 2.3 can now be resumed and closed

report.outcome: SPEC-0008: location capture, job tree, completion notice verified live. Drifts: bash lacks title/cwd, jobs list returns raw PascalCase Go JSON without command, wait needs id, missing states, foreground calls consume the finished-job retention. G8.20 spec text itself needs an http/https exemption. Recorded.

SPEC-0009: all top-level routes exist, but several specified subcommands (frames show/hide, prompt render/diff, skills load/unload, tools --format, jobs monitor) are absent, aliases are not canonicalized and verbs differ per family; the activity line lacks the state, instructions and location items and polls with I/O at 2 Hz. Recorded.
open: ask_user not exercised live (would interrupt the user); relying on the project's RPC live tests

report.outcome: SPEC-0010: layering, typed catalog, atomic 0600 saves (temp+fsync+rename, flock), malformed refusal and trust limits are implemented per spec and extending-pig invariant 7. The main gap is the already recorded 65/100 inert catalog keys (shown with application 'unavailable'); instructions.classes configuration is deferred by PLAN-0002.

SPEC-0011: endpoint discovery and agent tree verified live (5 peers listed); send/wake not exercised to avoid waking the user's other agents (covered by project live tests). Found: edit lock files accumulate without cleanup (131 files), small tree/column drifts.

SPEC-0012 live: artifact, local, cfg, job, agent trees list; retired schemes answer. HIGH: session root and by-id listings fail on a real machine because sessionProvider.List ignores the 16-entry page limit enforced by list.go. Session subtree lacks tree/messages/frames/instructions; skill tree excludes user-level skills; out root unsupported. Project registry/storage conversion not re-verified (covered by project tests).

SPEC-0013 live with synthetic random tokens in ~/.cache scratch: token shapes are redacted in read and bash results. Gap: an env file referenced by a tool call (read of a .env outside the cwd chain) is not learned, its KEY value reaches the model in plaintext, contrary to §2. Vault/ask-secret/env-injection not re-verified live (secrets.env-injection is an inert setting).

SPEC-0014 live: the system-prompt session resource is a hardcoded, stale one-line stub; host-discovered skills are not in the skill tree (only cwd-local skill dirs), so progressive disclosure covers almost no real skill; prompt.template is not wired. Engine, epochs, frames and the six context frames were observed working in this session's own context (date, environment, project, location, model, capabilities frames arrived once).

TUI review done; findings in ~/.cache/pig-workbench-test-tmp/findings-tui.md. Headline: frames render as raw envelopes in the transcript (no message renderer); tool rows uniform but unstyled and built by two parallel renderers; panels use single-key actions and hardcoded key names.

No glyphs, theme tokens or densities (chrome deferred to PLAN-0004). Own tools do not use the SPEC-0003 snapshot path. Findings appended to findings.md.

subtasks.title: Hub, panels and settings vs ui-ux.md and dashboard-standard.md

report.outcome: Hub and 16 panels captured live. Settings panel does have search, scope tab, provenance, takes-effect note and staged save (good).
Activity line and status segments work and fit widths; plain unstyled text, poll-driven goroutine outside the supervisor. Low-severity notes only.
